checkpoints.description: [1/3] argv builtins: argc() and arg_byte(i, j) over GetCommandLineA; [2/3] stdin read_char() with a 4096-byte buffered static in writable .data; [3/3] dedicated benchmark twins + benchmark gate

impact_assessment.why: the language cannot react to the outside world: no stdin, no args, only print builtins; input is the first step of a usable language per the agreed roadmap
impact_assessment.benefits: programs can consume argv and stdin; string handling becomes reachable; one import and one writable-data extension
impact_assessment.risks: contract: argv[0] is the program path (C convention) and read_char returns -1 on EOF; dependency: GetStdHandle and GetCommandLineA join the import table, and .data gains labels after the IAT; concurrency: none; state: static cursor/count live in .data, zero-initialized by the loader
impact_assessment.mitigation: failing-first sema/codegen/e2e tests per builtin; buffered reads mean one ReadFile per 4096 bytes; benchmark twin set pins throughput equivalence; keep the existing print ABI untouched

checkpoints.description: [3/3] Input builtins land: argc, arg_byte and read_char with the static argv cache and 4096-byte stdin buffer, writable .data region after the IAT, benchmark twins argv_walk and char_stream in the harness, 997 tests OK, gate exit 0. ADR-051.

[1/3] Plan: M1 exit(code) builtin via the already-linked ExitProcess; M2 string literals (lexed str tokens with \ \" \n \t escapes, NUL-terminated deduped .rodata storage, value = literal address as i64) plus str_len, str_byte, print_str builtins; M3 benchmark twin for string reads and delivery.

impact_assessment.why: programs cannot fail with a message or compare text: without exit a check can only return a code upward, and without literals every test fixture is unreachable; both are the smallest steps that make the test suite writable in Cairn
impact_assessment.benefits: assert-style helpers become writable Cara programs themselves: print_str + str_len + str_byte cover message output, length checks and fixture scanning; exit gives fail-fast semantics with a nonzero exit code
impact_assessment.risks: contract: a string literal's value is its bytes' address (i64-typed like everything else), str_byte answers -1 only for negative j and callers bound with str_len, reading past the NUL stays inside .rodata and is documented; dependency: none new (WriteFile/ExitProcess already imported), rodata gains NUL-terminated blobs; concurrency: none; state: literals live in the read-only section the loader already maps
impact_assessment.mitigation: failing-first tests at every layer (lexer escapes, sema arities and the exit-is-not-a-value rule, codegen shape, e2e assert helper and exit propagation); data-dependent benchmark twin so no optimizer may fold the read; keep builtins non-redefinable per the existing E3012 check

[3/3] Delivered: exit(code), string literals with print_str/str_len/str_byte, str_scan twin; 1068 tests OK; gate exit 0, no regressions (mandelbrot -18.6%, argv_walk -26.0%); str_scan cairn 18.5 vs C 12.4 vs C++ 12.4 vs Rust 30.5 ms

[1/4] Plan: close the recorded call-shape gaps. M1 investigate call_chain's unexplained 25% gap to C (42.4 vs 33.8 ms) and fix; M2 inline str_byte when the pointer is a known literal or home (str_scan 18.5 vs C 12.4); M3 improve argv_walk (30.1 vs C 20.1) by inlining arg_byte's bounds/cap checks; M4 gate + delivery. Benchmark gate re-runs after every change; failing-first tests per codegen change.

impact_assessment.why: the standing goal is faster-than-C on its own scoreboard: three cases have known mechanisms and a quarter of the call_chain gap is unexplained overhead that likely taxes every call-bearing program
impact_assessment.benefits: contract: no source-level semantics change, only lowerings; str_byte/arg_byte inlines keep identical -1 semantics and clobber rules; dependency: no new imports or sections, existing call-site machinery reused; concurrency: none; state: codegen-only, no static data unless an inline spills
impact_assessment.risks: contract: an inlined str_byte must reproduce NUL-check and -1 answers exactly, and peepholes must not disturb the delta/inline machinery; dependency: instruction encodings reused, low; concurrency: none; state: inline expansion may grow .text, bounded per call site
impact_assessment.mitigation: contract: codegen shape tests plus the full suite and e2e re-run after each milestone, and the --save --compare gate must exit 0 before any commit; dependency: machine.py helpers only, no hand-rolled bytes; concurrency: n/a; state: gate reports .text sizes for review

checkpoints.description: [3/3] Delivered: select-if reversed to lea, sub, cmov (call_chain -19.7%) and str_byte leaf-index inline (str_scan -10.1%); arg_byte inline and rcx-binding measured slower, recorded as dead ends; 1073 tests OK; gate exit 0

[1/4] Plan: close the remaining loop gaps. M1 binary_gcd (187 vs C 164 / Rust 139): diff the disassembly, find the per-iteration slack, fix; M2 nqueens (23.7 vs C 21.7 / Rust 17.6): try the recorded countdown-scan idea and any branching slack; M3 primes (24.1 vs Rust 18.4) and xorshift (287 vs C 278) peepholes as the gate data directs; M4 gate + delivery. Every fix ships a failing-first shape test; every change re-runs the --save --compare gate.

impact_assessment.why: the scoreboard still shows cairn behind C on binary_gcd, nqueens, primes, mandelbrot, xorshift and many_params; these are the same hot-loop constructs every real Cairn program leans on, so closing them raises the whole language
impact_assessment.benefits: contract: no source semantics change, only lowerings; identical results pinned by existing twin parity tests and e2e; dependency: machine.py helpers only; concurrency: none; state: codegen only, no new static data
impact_assessment.risks: contract: reordered or fused instructions must keep exact i64 wrap and flag semantics, or the parity tests catch it; dependency: low, existing encodings; concurrency: none; state: inline expansion may grow .text, bounded
impact_assessment.mitigation: contract: failing-first shape tests plus the 1073-suite and twin-parity after each milestone; the --save --compare gate must exit 0 before any commit; measured A/B against builds from the stashed tree; dependency: no hand-rolled bytes; concurrency: n/a; state: gate reports sizes
